★★★★½

I'm not a huge Bigfoot enthusiast, however I thoroughly enjoyed learning about the history, encounters, insights and theories that William Jevning recounted during this interview. Many topics were covered including audio of Bigfoot screams and photos of track casts were also examined. The interview was thoroughly engrossing and entertaining while also seeming relatively compelling.

If you are a Bigfoot devotee, I suspect you will love this!

Notes from the Midnight In The Desert website

http://midnightinthedesert.com/william-jevning/

William Jevning is a two time witness of Sasquatch encounters and veteran field researcher of these creatures. William was a long time close friend and protege' of world famous Sasquatch Hunter Rene' Dahinden. He is the author of "Notes From the Field, Tracking North America's Sasquatch", "The Minnesota Iceman", and "In Search of the Unknown". William also Studied Anthropology and Psychology at Washington State University.

Detailed Review

I was never used to be a huge fan of Bigfoot stories or cryptids until a few years ago when I gained an appreciation of how interesting and creepy a good hiking story can be, even without Sasquatch... and how often a good cryptid story will be intertwined with fascinating folklore and history from the region.

William Jevning has been researching, hunting and collecting Bigfoot evidence for over 40 years and he has some great stories to share about his experiences discovering and casting footprints, how he was introduced to some of the founding fathers of Bigfoot research, his theories on Bigfoot structures such as huge rock formations, pits and twisted trees trunks.

Jevning discusses the famous 1967 Patterson–Gimlin Bigfoot video footage, compares the authenticity of the video against his research into the most advanced special effects of the last 1960's that was used by Walt Disney when filming the original Planet Of The Apes films and he even has a fun Bigfoot-related story about Patterson spending some time in prison that I hadn't heard of before!

One of Jevning's stories involves Park Rangers discovering the remains of a number of elk that had their heads removed without a cutting tool... but were torn off. :-)

Jevning also shares a number of audio clips of Bigfoot screams he record during his investigations and he refers to a number of awesome photos of Bigfoot and animal track casts he made during his travels too, which has been seen at the Midnight In The Desert's page for this episode and at William Jevning's website.

Jevning had a great radio voice and he never seemed unable to provide details without hesitation to Heather Wade's questions, which made suspension of disbelief much easier as he described his experiences in a calm, no-spin, matter-of-fact manner with plenty of details about times, dates, locations and other witnesses.

It's been many months since I had a chance to listen to MITD, however Heather Wade sounded much better than I remember, more relaxed and organized and she even shared her own possible Sasquatch story during the show, which was surprisingly interesting.

This was one of my favorite Bigfoot interviews, not necessarily a classic, but it covered many interesting topics and was fascinating from beginning to end with recounts that didn't seem like fiction from a Hollywood script.
